lines.text: Your first agent finishes the code. Then everything stops, because somebody has to start the reviewer.
That somebody is you. You check the board, copy the context, and open a new task. Every handoff.
Events close that gap. An event is just a named signal, like code changed.
When a task completes, it can emit that signal. The agent calls nothing. It just says what happened.
Wire the event to a workspace, and Agent R Q creates a task there on its own.
The reviewer is already listening. The moment the signal lands, it picks the task up and starts.
It chains. The reviewer emits its own event, then testing wakes up, then deploy.
You stay in control. Every workspace keeps its approvals, so a chain never skips a human.
Add a schedule, and a nightly build runs the whole release train while you sleep.
Every handoff shows up in the task timeline, so you can see what fired what, and when.
No glue code, no copy and paste. Try events at Agent R Q dot com.
